claims.claim: A CR is a temporary appropriations law funding the government at a rate the CR sets while regular bills are unfinished
claims.sourceSpan: a continuing resolution (often referred to simply as “CR”) may be enacted in a bill or joint resolution to provide funding for the affected agencies for the full year, up to a specified date, or until their regular appropriations are enacted

claims.claim: Since FY1977 all regular appropriations bills have been enacted before the fiscal year started only four times, most recently FY1997
claims.sourceSpan: Since FY1977, there have been four times when all regular appropriations bills have been enacted before the start of the fiscal year, most recently for FY1997

claims.claim: In recent practice the CR funding rate is based on the prior year’s appropriations acts, prorated for the CR’s duration
claims.sourceSpan: at the rate based on the prior year’s appropriations acts, prorated for the duration of the CR

claims.claim: VERBATIM QUOTE: H.R. 9770 funds continuing projects and activities "at a rate for operations as provided in the applicable appropriations Acts for fiscal year 2026 and under the authority and conditions provided in such Acts"
claims.sourceSpan: at a rate for operations as provided in the applicable appropriations Acts for fiscal year 2026 and under the authority and conditions provided in such Acts

claims.claim: Under H.R. 9770 funding for a program runs until the first of: a regular FY2027 appropriation for it is enacted; a FY2027 appropriations act is enacted without provision for it; or December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: until whichever of the following first occurs: (1) The enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this Act. (2) The enactment into law of the applicable appropriations Act for fiscal year 2027 without any provision for such project or activity. (3) December 4, 2026.

claims.claim: CRs carry "anomalies": additional provisions giving specific programs additional funding, exceptions to the CR’s terms and conditions, or other legislative changes
claims.sourceSpan: additional provisions (commonly referred to as “anomalies”) that provide either additional funding, exceptions to the terms and conditions of the CR, or other legislative changes for specific programs or activities

claims.claim: A minibus is consolidated appropriations legislation containing only some of the regular appropriations bills — full-year funding, not temporary funding
claims.sourceSpan: (Consolidated appropriations legislation containing only some of the regular appropriations bills may also be referred to as a “minibus.”)
claims.note: THE FIX: the pre-refresh article described a minibus as a type of CR ("a minibus CR — covering only some of the twelve appropriations subcommittees"). The stored CRS definition contradicts that; corrected in this refresh. Corrections-entry decision flagged for James.

claims.claim: VERBATIM QUOTE: H.R. 9770 bars its funding authority from being "used to initiate or resume any project or activity for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were not available during fiscal year 2026"
claims.sourceSpan: shall be used to initiate or resume any project or activity for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were not available during fiscal year 2026

claims.claim: Under a CR, unfunded programs stay unfunded and grown programs stay at the prior-year rate unless an anomaly provides otherwise
claims.sourceSpan: at a rate for operations as provided in the applicable appropriations Acts for fiscal year 2026
claims.note: Objective consequence of the rate provision (rate.hr9770.quote) plus the new-starts bar (newstarts.quote) and the anomalies mechanism (anomalies).

claims.claim: The federal fiscal year begins October 1
claims.sourceSpan: beginning with FY1977, fiscal years would commence on October 1 of each year and end on September 30

claims.claim: There are twelve regular appropriations bills, one per Appropriations subcommittee
claims.sourceSpan: organized in 12 subcommittees, with each subcommittee responsible for developing and managing the consideration of one regular appropriations act
claims.note: Row added after audit pass 1 (coverage note).

claims.claim: In every other fiscal year since FY1977, at least some of the regular bills were not in place when the fiscal year began
claims.sourceSpan: Since FY1977, there have been four times when all regular appropriations bills have been enacted before the start of the fiscal year, most recently for FY1997
claims.note: Logical complement of the sourced four-times fact — reworded after pass 1 flagged the prior "running on a CR" phrasing as overstating the source (a gap year can be a shutdown, not a CR).

claims.claim: FY2026 opened under a CR: H.R. 5371, signed November 12, 2025
claims.sourceSpan: Public Law 119-37 | HR 5371 | 2025-11-12 | Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construc

claims.claim: H.R. 5371 also carried three of the twelve regular bills as full-year divisions
claims.sourceSpan: Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2026 (division C of Public Law 119-37)
claims.note: Re-derivable: grep "Public Law 119-37" in the EH text’s Sec. 101 enumeration — divisions B (Agriculture/FDA), C (Legislative Branch), D (Military Construction/VA) = three regular acts.

claims.claim: A three-bill minibus followed in January: H.R. 6938, Public Law 119-74, January 23, 2026
claims.note: Three-act count re-derivable: grep "Public Law 119-74" in bill-119-hr-9770-eh.txt Sec. 101 enumeration = 3 divisions.

claims.claim: The five-division Consolidated Appropriations Act arrived February 3, 2026 (Public Law 119-75)
claims.sourceSpan: Public Law 119-75 | HR 7148 | 2026-02-03 | Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
claims.note: Five-division count re-derivable: grep "Public Law 119-75" in bill-119-hr-9770-eh.txt Sec. 101 enumeration = 5.

claims.claim: February 3 is more than four months into a fiscal year that began October 1
claims.note: Objective date arithmetic: Oct 1 → Feb 3 = 4 months 2 days; FY start sourced at default.oct1.

claims.claim: Homeland Security was finished last, April 30, 2026 (H.R. 7147, Public Law 119-86)
claims.sourceSpan: Public Law 119-86 | HR 7147 | 2026-04-30 | Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026.

claims.claim: VERBATIM QUOTE: the Consolidated Appropriations Act makes appropriations "for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026"
claims.sourceSpan: Making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes.

claims.claim: The House passed H.R. 9770 on July 21, 2026, 220-205 (Roll 272)
claims.sourceSpan: On passage Passed by the Yeas and Nays: 220 - 205 (Roll no. 272)

claims.claim: H.R. 9770 would continue funding at FY2026 rates from the start of the fiscal year until at latest December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: (3) December 4, 2026.
claims.note: Rate from rate.hr9770.quote; start of fiscal year = Oct 1 per default.oct1; latest end date this span.

resolution: First refresh of a frozen 2026-07-17 pre-lane explainer, full audit lane per D4. Trigger: the omnibus-vs-minibus session found a live definitional error (minibus described as a partial-coverage CR; the stored CRS definition is consolidated legislation containing only some regular bills) that also contradicted the new live sibling article. Rewrite fixes the definition, replaces the unsourced "lesser of House-passed or Senate-passed" rate formula with the sourced R47106 description plus H.R. 9770’s actual Sec. 101 text, drops the unsourced 1977/1989/1995/1997 year enumeration for the sourced four-times-most-recently-FY1997 fact, drops the unsourced multi-year-contracts/hiring bullets, and adds the receipt-bound FY2026 timeline and the September status section (per the amended RULE 2: receipt-bound examples). Heavy source reuse from the omnibus-vs-minibus retrofit (CRS/GAO/bill texts already stored).
notes: Pre-refresh errors REMOVED, not softened: minibus-as-CR definition (contradicted by CRS IN12324); the "lesser of the House-passed or Senate-passed level" rate formula (no stored source; the only lesser-of clause in H.R. 9770 concerns rescissions); the specific years 1977/1989/1995/1997 (stored source states four times / most recently FY1997 without enumerating); the multi-year-contract and hiring restriction bullets (unsourced operational glosses).
Corrections-entry decision for the minibus misdefinition flagged for James (material definitional error, live since May).

Audit pass 1 (Sonnet, hostile): 0 errors / 3 warn / 1 note. Fixes: IN12324 added to the Key Sources box; "every other year ran on a CR" reworded to the sourced complement (a gap year can be a shutdown, not a CR); the coverage paragraph reworded to navigational form and its weak process row dropped (pass-1 scoping: self-referential site behavior is not a sourced claim); default.twelve row added.
